\noindent Pre-specified sensitivity analyses (doublet-flagged cells excluded), the
pre-specified cap-robustness check (run with the memory-efficient block-wise Sinkhorn
solver) and per-replicate coupling recovery (Tables~S1--S5).
Tables~S6--S21 report exploratory analyses added after peer review in two rounds
(S6--S13 and S14--S21). Their settings were fixed in dated entries of the analysis plan
before any of them was run; they were not part of the original plan. Two were reduced in
size before they were run to fit the available computing: in Table~S17 the random forest
uses 10 of the 50 target draws, and Table~S16 uses 20 seeds with each half capped at
4{,}000 cells. Primary cell set throughout.
All values are generated from the saved per-cell and per-seed result files.

\section*{Supplementary methods: post-review analyses}
Partner error, $R$, is defined in the main text. Notation follows the main text: $C_{ij}$ is the median-scaled cost, $w_{ij}$ the row-normalised coupling, $\mathcal{A}$ the set of admissible training targets.

\emph{Proximity baselines.} kNN couplings with $k\in\{5,10,20,50\}$, a row-normalised
Gaussian kernel $w_{ij}\propto\exp(-C_{ij}/\varepsilon)$ without column constraint
($\varepsilon\in\{0.01,0.05,0.1\}$), and mutual nearest neighbours ($k=10$) were scored with
the RQ1 metrics plus average precision (AP; chance $s_i/n$).

\emph{Structured partners in RQ4.} Per seed, the stage-III cells are split at random into a
control and a treated half (each capped at 4{,}000 cells; 20 seeds). Treated cells receive
the effect of the main-text RQ4 simulation; each is paired with a control cell that is random, sampled from
its kNN ($k=10$) or OT row ($\varepsilon=0.05$, fitted between the halves in their own 30-PC
space), or the row average (barycentric). The same linear and a sparse effect are used.

\emph{Training targets in RQ2.} For OT and independent pairs we compare the sampled target
of the main-text RQ2 design with the row-weighted mean target, each with $\mathcal{A}$ either
as before or restricted to later cells of training clones, for both the (Pg, D) and the
30-PC input. Sampled designs use 50 draws per split (10 for the random forest).

\emph{Other spaces and growth.} OT ($\varepsilon=0.05$) and kNN were recomputed with 15 or
50 PCs and with 4{,}000 HVGs. Growth-informed OT replaces $\mathbf{a}$ by
$a_i\propto\exp(\lambda\tilde g_i)$, $\lambda\in\{0.5,1\}$, where $\tilde g_i$ is the
standardised mean expression of the S-phase and G2/M genes of~\cite{Tirosh_2016}, balanced
and unbalanced.

\emph{Fate labels.} Label transfer is scored by leave-one-clone-out accuracy on the authors'
labels, and OT-minus-reference TVD differences get paired clone-bootstrap intervals, with all
labels and with measured labels only.

\emph{Second dataset.} LARRY in vitro haematopoiesis~\cite{Weinreb_2020} (GEO GSE140802)
barcodes progenitors and profiles their clones on days 2, 4 and 6. A clone is a barcode,
and the transitions are day 2$\to$4 and 4$\to$6. The deposited counts are already
normalised, so expression is $\log(1+x)$ of them, with 2{,}000 HVGs (library as batch) and
30 PCs. Each transition uses three pools, each a subsample of whole cross-stage clones (at
most 6{,}000 foreground cells per day) plus background, 8{,}000 cells per day. The pools
stand in for replicates but are not biological replicates. Couplings and metrics are as
above; fate agreement uses the authors' annotation of every cell, with no label transfer.

\emph{CellRank 2.} A real-time kernel built from the balanced OT plan
($\varepsilon=0.05$), with within-stage connectivity kernels (weight 0.2), gives
fate probabilities towards the later fate classes~\cite{Weiler_2024}. They are scored by TVD
and, without fitting, as an RQ3 predictor on the same test clones.
